t: A square touchscreen on a metal stand that you program with Wi-Fi projects.
steps: Buy Presto from Pimoroni, Adafruit, or The Pi Hut, or pick the Starter Kit for extra sensors.
Plug it into your computer with a USB-C data cable.
Try the built-in launcher and tap through a few examples.
Install the free Thonny editor on your computer.
Set Thonny to the MicroPython for Raspberry Pi Pico option.
Stop the running launcher in Thonny and open a short example.
Try a Wi-Fi example from the Presto examples repo.
Update the firmware from the Pimoroni guide on an early beta unit.
meta: Open Board. From $77. A few stores.
